draft.title: Psychological strategies
card: Athletes set clear targets, such as a time to beat or a skill to master, to give training direction and keep them motivated.
The athlete pictures a skill or event in their mind, using sight, sound and feel, to rehearse it before they perform.
This is the words an athlete says to themselves. Short, positive cues such as "smooth and steady" can keep them focused and confident.
Methods such as slow breathing lower tension and nerves. Concentration skills help an athlete focus on what matters and ignore distractions.
draft.remember: Psychological strategies train the mind so an athlete can handle pressure and perform well.

a.q: Before a free throw, a basketballer closes her eyes and pictures the ball leaving her hand and dropping through the hoop. Which strategy is this?
a.why: She is rehearsing the skill by picturing it in her mind, which is imagery. Self-talk is tempting, but it uses words said to oneself, and she is using pictures.
a.clue: She is using pictures in her mind, not words.

b.q: Tom, a swimmer, feels his heart pounding before a final. He breathes slowly to calm down, then repeats "long strokes, strong finish" to himself. Which two strategies is he using?
b.why: Slow breathing to lower tension is relaxation. Repeating a short phrase to himself is self-talk. He pictures nothing and sets no target, so imagery and goal setting do not fit.
b.clue: One act calms the body and the other uses words.

problems.detail: Concentration skills are a separate strategy named in this point, but the card tucks them into the 'Relaxation' bullet. Students may think concentration is a type of relaxation. Give it its own bullet.

proposal.title: Psychological strategies
card: Goal setting means setting clear targets, such as a time to beat or a skill to master. It gives training direction and keeps motivation up.
Imagery is rehearsing a skill or event in the mind before doing it, using the sight, sound and feel of the movement.
Concentration skills help an athlete keep attention on the task, such as the ball or the race plan, and block out distractions like a noisy crowd.
Self-talk is the words athletes say to themselves, such as "smooth and steady". Relaxation methods, such as slow breathing, lower tension and nerves.
proposal.remember: Psychological strategies train the mind so an athlete can handle pressure and perform well.

a.q: Before a free throw, a basketballer shuts her eyes and runs through the shot in her head: the release, the arc, the ball dropping through the hoop. Which strategy is this?
a.why: She mentally rehearses the whole shot before taking it, using the sight and feel of the movement. That is imagery. Concentration skills are tempting, but they keep attention on the task and block distractions rather than rehearse a skill.
a.clue: She has not taken the shot yet, but she is already doing it.

b.q: Tom, a swimmer, feels his heart pounding before a final. He breathes slowly to calm down, then repeats "long strokes, strong finish" to himself. Which two strategies is he using?
b.why: Slow breathing to lower tension is relaxation. Repeating a short phrase to himself is self-talk. He does not rehearse the race in his mind or set a target, so imagery and goal setting do not fit.
b.clue: One act calms the body and the other uses words.
